benchmark.name: Prefix-cache multi-turn agent trace
benchmark.task: Interleaved K=5-session x T=5-turn synthetic agentic conversation, SHARED vs CONTROL system-prompt conditions, TTFT measured per (engine, condition, turn)
benchmark.dataset: Deterministic synthetic tool-catalog + agent trace, seed=1729, 150 requests/engine (5 sessions x 5 turns x 3 trials)
benchmark.metric: TTFT p50, SHARED condition, turn 5 (longest shared+growing prefix)
benchmark.setup: Qwen2.5-3B, single RTX 3060 Ti 8GB, vLLM 0.23.0 (--enable-prefix-caching, AWQ-Marlin) / SGLang 0.5.9 (RadixAttention default, AWQ-Marlin) / Ollama 0.30.10 (default, GGUF q4_K_M), --enforce-eager/--disable-cuda-graph, mem-fraction 0.50, sequential requests (concurrency=1)
benchmark.reproduction_command: bash harness/run_engine_prefix.sh vllm && bash harness/run_engine_prefix.sh sglang && bash harness/run_engine_prefix.sh ollama && python3 harness/aggregate_multiturn.py results/vllm.csv results/sglang.csv results/ollama.csv --outdir results/agg

leaderboard.notes: Fastest at turn 5 shared-condition TTFT p50; effectively tied with SGLang (1.09x gap, overlapping p95: 0.1554s vs 0.1320s)
Statistical tie with vLLM at turn 5 -- refutes this battle's stated hypothesis of a 6.4x SGLang advantage over vLLM on prefix caching
3.25x slower than vLLM regardless of shared vs control condition; different quantization (GGUF q4_K_M vs AWQ-Marlin, disclosed boundary)

hypothesis.statement: SGLang's RadixAttention delivers a sustained 6.4x prefix-cache TTFT advantage over vLLM's Automatic Prefix Caching at the longest shared prefix

cost.note: Self-estimated authoring cost (Claude Sonnet 5, main thread + one forked subagent building the harness/running trials); measurement runs themselves cost $0 (local hardware, no API calls to any LLM provider)
